**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve chained commands after managed programs**

When an existing hook starts with a managed script but chains user behavior, such as `~/.claude/hooks/format-edited-files.py && ~/bin/audit-edit.sh`, this predicate classifies the entire hook object as managed because it checks only the first token. `merge_managed_entries` then removes the whole object, silently deleting the user's audit hook on the next apply; restrict recognition to an exact managed invocation or preserve any chained command segment. The threat-table claim that every unmanaged PostToolUse hook is retained is therefore not closed by the current wrapper/custom-hook tests.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L78-L78](https://github.com/mryfmo/dotfiles/blob/5bcab1f98c60ff6043422794b1c1a72483edb1ac/AGENTS.md#L78-L78)

items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Match managed hook paths instead of basenames**

When a user has an unrelated single-token PostToolUse command such as `/opt/team/format-edited-files.py` (or invokes it through a recognized interpreter), this basename-only check classifies it as managed, so `merge_managed_entries` removes the user hook and substitutes the repository-managed entry on the next `chezmoi apply`. This contradicts the threat-table claim that every unmanaged PostToolUse hook is retained; match the expected managed path rather than every executable sharing the basename.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L78-L78](https://github.com/mryfmo/dotfiles/blob/72d0e66dcf27bfdb1161f4f4f52b35ef3857b928/AGENTS.md#L78-L78)

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Limit matching to the actual managed hook location**

When a user-level entry invokes an unrelated project or team script such as `/workspace/team/.claude/hooks/format-edited-files.py`, this regex accepts it because any prefix ending in `/.claude/hooks/<managed basename>` is considered managed; `merge_managed_entries` then removes that user hook and substitutes the repository-managed entry on the next apply. Although the prior plain `/opt/team/format-edited-files.py` case is fixed, the new unrestricted `.claude/hooks` suffix is fresh evidence of the same user-hook loss; restrict matching to `~/.claude/hooks` and known managed home paths rather than every project-local `.claude/hooks` directory. The threat-table claim that every unmanaged PostToolUse hook is retained therefore remains unclosed.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L78-L78](https://github.com/mryfmo/dotfiles/blob/e5d0141bfe63f3bcb558631731785d6f92a92080/AGENTS.md#L78-L78)
